description.en: 170 km coastal route from Ise Grand Shrine to Kumano Hayatama Taisha. A series of 20+ mountain passes connecting fishing villages along the eastern coast of the Kii Peninsula. Typically 9-14 days.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.notes: Relation 19693803 is the confirmed Iseji — see the osm block below for why it is pinned even though no walked line ships from it this release.

osm.note: Confirmed as the Iseji: wikidata=Q11379141, wikipedia=ja:伊勢路 (熊野古道), and it is Mie Prefecture's own Kumano Kodō site (https://www.kodo.pref.mie.lg.jp/). Pinned here even though this section ships without geometry, so the next attempt starts from a confirmed id rather than repeating a day of research. The relation holds only two ways — 120679201 (1.32 km) and 1128207928 (0.74 km), 2.06 km total against a roughly 170 km route — in two components 22.3 km apart (Kii-Nagashima and the Owase/Kumano-shi area). That is an upstream OpenStreetMap gap, not a wrong id: a corridor-wide sweep for the classic Iseji pass names turns up only about 10 km more of loose, unrelated ways, nowhere near enough to assemble a walked line. ways: null until OpenStreetMap fills in what is missing.
